# PR #2056: Patch: audio comes back cleanly after a phone backgrounds the browser mid-game

Closes #2034

## What changed and why

The engine never reacted to the page lifecycle: `unlock()` called `resume()` on a context the OS had closed (rejection swallowed, nothing rebuilt — permanent silence), and anything scheduled against a frozen clock plus the music focus gain fired all at once on resume (the tear). Changes, all in `apps/web/src/audio/`:

- [engine.ts](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2034/apps/web/src/audio/engine.ts): new `LifecyclePort` type and `browserLifecycle()` (`visibilitychange` + `pagehide`/`pageshow`), subscribed on creation and removed in `dispose()`. Hidden cuts the voice channel via the existing `silenceVoice()` and records nothing else; visible rebuilds a closed context, then runs `startNext()` and `notifyState()`. `unlock()` now tears down a closed graph (settings unsubscribe, voice silence, duck/sfx windows, decoded-voice cache; byte cache kept) and builds a fresh context, mix and settings subscription before resuming. `begin()`/`startNext()` refuse to take the channel while hidden, and `onLoaded()`/`speakNow()` end the line as `"suspended"` when the context is not running, so post-timer and post-fetch callbacks can no longer schedule a backlog burst. Disconnect cleanups in `later()` are untouched.
- [music.ts](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2034/apps/web/src/audio/music.ts): `applyFocus()` now calls `cancelScheduledValues(now)` before the existing `setTargetAtTime(target, now, MUSIC_FOCUS_TC_S)`, so every resume is a ramp, never a jump. `ensureGraph()` clears the decoded-music cache on a context change (dead-context buffers are what the strict fake forbids) and resets `appliedFocus` to `null` there, so the first `sync()` after a rebuild always re-issues the ramp. First-graph creation is unchanged (starts at its level, no spurious ramp event).
- [types.ts](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2034/apps/web/src/audio/types.ts): `contextsCreated()` doc no longer says "(0 or 1)".
- Tests: 4 in `engine.test.ts` (closed-context rebuild with mix + settings proof, `interrupted`→`suspended`→resume, hidden refusals plus resolving-fetch-while-hidden starts nothing, visible-again gesture resumes and SFX reaches the sfx bus), 2 in `music.test.ts` (wanted track restarts on the new context with focus back at 1; focus loss/resume ends in `cancelScheduledValues` + `setTargetAtTime` to 1 over `MUSIC_FOCUS_TC_S` with no `setValueAtTime`/`linearRamp` jump), 1 in `unlock.test.ts` (gesture while `closed` calls `unlock`).

No ruling and no spec change: all of this is §10.11 "Autoplay"/"Music"/"Settings" conformance. No engine, cards, AI or server crate touched.

## How it was tested

- `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/audio/engine.test.ts` — 90 passed (4 new, confirmed by name in verbose output).
- `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/audio/music.test.ts src/audio/unlock.test.ts` — 52 passed (3 new, confirmed by name).
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` — clean (after `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` rebuilt the WASM packages).
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean; `cargo jackioh spec check` — ok (1262 rulings, 2890 proofs); `eslint` on the six touched files — clean.
- Worktree holds only the six intended modifications; no extra worktrees.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- Cutting the voice channel on hide drops a mid-utterance line instead of pausing it: pausing is impossible on a suspended context, and resuming mid-line would desynchronise the one-channel queue. Rejected: letting the line finish while hidden, which is exactly the backlog path.
- Clearing decoded voice/music caches on rebuild costs one re-fetch plus re-decode per backgrounding; the compressed-bytes caches are kept, so no extra network beyond a fresh decode. Rejected: reusing dead-context `AudioBuffer`s, which the strict fake forbids and which risks stale-buffer playback.
- The exact physical tear per phone OS cannot be reproduced in jsdom, so the tests pin the observable contract (cancel plus re-ramp, no backlog scheduling) rather than a per-OS cause.
- Departures from the plan, all behavior-preserving: the `contextsCreated()` doc fix lives in `types.ts` though the file list said not to touch it; `speakAfter()` needed no separate guard because it never touches speech/duck itself and the `speakNow()` check covers every path into them; engine test 4 uses the default run-mode factory plus a manual suspend, since a `stay` factory could never reach `running` via `unlock()`.

## Look twice

- `onLifecycle()` runs outside a gesture, so it rebuilds but deliberately never resumes: after a visible-with-closed-context return, `state()` stays `"suspended"` until the next tap, which is what makes the iOS gesture requirement hold.
- In-flight `decode()`/`decoding` jobs captured the old context and can still land a dead-context buffer into the cleared caches after a rebuild; the plan did not ask to close that hole and no test covers it, so a backgrounding raced with a decode remains a residual risk worth a follow-up.

### Adversarial review

Approved on round 1 of 3.

Notes the reviewer left (not blocking):

- `apps/web/src/audio/engine.ts`: SFX and duck automation scheduled just before hiding are not cancelled on hide, so a delayed cue can still land on resume.
- `apps/web/src/audio/music.ts`: An in-flight music decode that resolves after a rebuild can store a dead-context buffer into the cleared cache.
- `apps/web/src/audio/engine.test.ts`: The interrupted-context test proves resume to running but not audible SFX/music restart for that state.

```text
# #2034: Patch: audio comes back cleanly after a phone backgrounds the browser mid-game
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

### What happens

This is a recent regression. On a phone, during a game, leaving the browser (switching to another app or the home screen) and then coming back does one of two things every time:

1. **The audio never comes back.** Music, SFX and voice all stay silent for the rest of the game, even after more taps.
2. **A loud, harsh audio tear** (a crackle, glitch or burst) plays as the page comes back.

It reproduces every time on mobile. It was not happening before the last few days of audio changes.

### What should happen

When the page comes back to the foreground, sound picks up where it left off. If the OS left the context suspended, the next tap resumes it (`apps/web/src/audio/unlock.ts`'s contract: "iOS can suspend the context again after a call or a backgrounding, and the next tap has to resume it"). Nothing that was scheduled or held while the page was hidden plays as a burst, and the music fades back in on its focus ramp (`MUSIC_FOCUS_TC_S`) with no click.

### How to reproduce

1. On a phone (iOS Safari and/or Android Chrome), open the client and start a game (`/practice` is enough). Tap until sound plays.
2. Mid-game, with music playing, leave the browser: go to the home screen or switch apps for a few seconds or longer.
3. Come back to the browser and tap the board.
4. Either nothing is audible from then on, or a harsh tear plays as the page returns.

### Where

`apps/web`, `apps/web/src/audio/`

### Leads (unconfirmed: verify before acting on them)

- `engine.ts` doesn't react to the page's lifecycle (`visibilitychange`, `pagehide`/`pageshow`, the context's `statechange`). Only the music player's focus gain (`music.ts` `browserFocus`) and the gesture unlock (`unlock.ts`) do. Everything else is left to the OS suspending and resuming the context.
- `unlock()` (`engine.ts`) only calls `ctx.resume()` on the existing context. If the OS closed it while the page was in the background (or it came back from the bfcache in a state `resume()` can't fix), nothing ever builds a new one. That would explain "audio doesn't come back". `state()` maps Safari's `"interrupted"` to `"suspended"`, so look at that path too.
- For the tear: anything scheduled against `ctx.currentTime` or by `setTimeout` while the page was hidden (music voices and fades, ducks, SFX, the focus gain's `setTargetAtTime`) may all fire or jump at once when the context resumes. Also check whether a gain ramp starts from a stale value.
- Recent audio changes to bisect from: #1887 (the #1827 build, the page-wide `appAudio.ts`, unlock and menu music) and #1970 (`engine.ts`'s `RAPID_SFX` field taps). Neither is confirmed as the cause.

### Acceptance

- Unit tests in `apps/web/src/audio/` with a fake `AudioContext` and document. The page goes hidden, then visible again, with the context `suspended`, `interrupted` and `closed`. After the next gesture, `engine.state()` is `"running"` and `playSfx` and the music play again. A closed context is rebuilt along with its mix and settings subscription.
- A test that nothing scheduled while the page was hidden plays as a backlog on resume, and that the music's focus gain ramps back from silence instead of jumping.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm --dir apps/web test` pass.
- No change to the engine, cards, AI or server crates.

### Version or commit

Seen on production around 2026-10-27, `main` at or after `5e04fd9`.

Guard every subscription callback body with the file's existing `try/catch`-swallow convention only where the surrounding code already swallows; lifecycle callbacks must never throw into the page.
4. Rewrite `unlock()`'s closed-context path in `engine.ts`: today a closed `ctx` falls through to `ctx.resume()`, whose rejection is swallowed and nothing is ever rebuilt. Update the `contextsCreated()` doc comment ("How many AudioContexts this engine has constructed"), which currently says "(0 or 1)".
5. In `engine.ts`, close the stale-scheduling holes so nothing queued while hidden plays as a backlog: at the top of `begin()` and `startNext()`, return early when `!accepting()` (a timer that fires while hidden must not take the channel; `noteVisible`'s `startNext()` in step 3 picks the queue up). In `onLoaded()`, extend the existing early return to also return unless `running()` is true, ending the line with the existing `finish(ch, "suspended")` path used for not-running accepts. In `speakAfter()`/`speakNow()`, check `running()` (not just at request time) before touching `speech` or calling `duck()`/`duckSfx()`. Do not change the `later()` helper itself: disconnect cleanups must still run.
6. In `apps/web/src/audio/music.ts`, fix `applyFocus()` so the resume is always a ramp from silence: before the existing `setTargetAtTime(target, graph.ctx.currentTime, MUSIC_FOCUS_TC_S)`, call `graph.focus.gain.cancelScheduledValues(now)` with the same `now`; never use `setValueAtTime` or a linear ramp to 1 on the focus gain. Keep the `if (target === appliedFocus) return;` early-out, and additionally reset `appliedFocus` to `null` whenever the engine reports a new context (the existing `ensureGraph()` early branch where `graph.ctx !== out.context`), so the first `sync()` after a rebuild always re-issues the ramp even if the wanted value equals the cached one.
7. In `music.ts` `ensureGraph()`'s context-change branch (which already clears `voices`, `clip`, `pendingIntro` and `introDecoded`), also clear the `decoded` music-buffer cache: the buffers were decoded by the dead context and must be re-decoded on the new one. Keep the `bytes` cache, `resumeAt` offsets, `failed` set and `want` request untouched so the wanted track restarts where it left off via the existing `subscribeState(() => quietly(sync))` path.
8. Add the `engine.test.ts` tests using the existing `rig()`/`elapse()`/`settle()` helpers plus a fake lifecycle port (`{ visible: boolean; fire(): void }` mirroring `music.test.ts`'s fake focus port). Wire it through a new `lifecycle` option on `rig()`. Assert on `FakeAudio.startedSources()`, `paramLog`/`targets()`, `nodesOf()`, `engine.log()` outcomes (`"suspended"` is already in `VoiceOutcome`), and `violations` equals `[]`.
9. Add the `music.test.ts` tests using its existing `rig()` with an injectable focus port and the real engine over `fakeContextFactory`. Assert focus-gain `ParamEvent`s end with `cancelScheduledValues` then `setTargetAtTime` to 1 at the resumed `currentTime` with time constant `MUSIC_FOCUS_TC_S`, and that no `setValueAtTime`/`linearRampToValueAtTime` to 1 touches the focus gain.
10. Add the `unlock.test.ts` closed-state test with the existing `rig()`/`install()`/`gesture()` helpers: build the engine, close the fake context (`audio.state = "closed"`), dispatch a gesture, and assert `engine.unlock` was called (the listener already calls through for `"closed"` since it only skips `"running"`/`"unsupported"`).

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/audio/engine.test.ts`: `background: unlock() after the OS closed the context builds a new context, mix and settings subscription` (close the fake, `unlock()`, assert `factory.create` called twice, `contextsCreated()` 2, `state()` `"running"`, a later `writeAudioSettings` reaches the new buses via `setTargetAtTime`, `playSfx("draw")` true and logged, `violations` empty); `background: an interrupted context reads suspended and resumes on the next gesture` (set `state = "interrupted"`, assert `state()` `"suspended"`, `playSfx` accepted and logged, `unlock()` returns to `"running"`); `background: cues requested while hidden are refused and timers that fire while hidden never take the channel` (hide via the fake lifecycle port, assert `playSfx`/`playVoice` false with empty log, resolve a hanging fetch while hidden, elapse, assert no started sources and a free channel); `background: after visible again the next gesture resumes and playSfx plays through the sfx bus` (suspend with `resumeMode: "stay"`, hide, show and fire, `unlock()`, assert running and a started source reaching the sfx bus).
- `apps/web/src/audio/music.test.ts`: `background: after the context is closed and rebuilt, the wanted track starts on the new context` (request a track, close the fake engine context, `engine.unlock()`, settle, assert the new fake context owns started voices through the music chain and the focus target ends at 1); `background: focus loss then resume re-issues the focus ramp from silence` (unfocus and fire, suspend, refocus/fire plus `unlock()`, settle, assert the focus gain's last events are `cancelScheduledValues` then `setTargetAtTime` to 1 at the resumed `currentTime` with `MUSIC_FOCUS_TC_S`, and no `setValueAtTime`/`linearRampToValueAtTime` to 1 on it).
- `apps/web/src/audio/unlock.test.ts`: `background: a gesture while the engine reports closed calls unlock so the tap rebuilds` (stub engine `{ unlock, state: () => "closed" }`, gesture, assert called once).
- Commands: `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`, then `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/audio/engine.test.ts`, `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/audio/music.test.ts`, `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/audio/unlock.test.ts`, then `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] Hidden-then-visible with `suspended`, `interrupted` and `closed` contexts: after the next gesture `state()` is `"running"` and `playSfx` plus the music play again.
- [ ] A closed context is rebuilt with a new mix and settings subscription; the wanted music track restarts on the new context from its resume point.
- [ ] Nothing scheduled while hidden plays as a backlog on resume; the focus gain ramps back from silence over `MUSIC_FOCUS_TC_S` with no jump.
- [ ] The three audio test files, `typecheck` and `spec check` pass; no engine, cards, AI or server crate changed; no ruling added.

- Clearing the decoded voice/music caches on rebuild costs one re-fetch plus re-decode per backgrounding; the compressed-bytes caches are kept, so no extra network beyond what a fresh decode needs. Rejected alternative: reusing dead-context `AudioBuffer`s, which the strict fake forbids and which risks stale-buffer playback.

# #2034: Patch: audio comes back cleanly after a phone backgrounds the browser mid-game
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

### What happens

This is a recent regression. On a phone, during a game, leaving the browser (switching to another app or the home screen) and then coming back does one of two things every time:

1. **The audio never comes back.** Music, SFX and voice all stay silent for the rest of the game, even after more taps.
2. **A loud, harsh audio tear** (a crackle, glitch or burst) plays as the page comes back.

It reproduces every time on mobile. It was not happening before the last few days of audio changes.

### What should happen

When the page comes back to the foreground, sound picks up where it left off. If the OS left the context suspended, the next tap resumes it (`apps/web/src/audio/unlock.ts`'s contract: "iOS can suspend the context again after a call or a backgrounding, and the next tap has to resume it"). Nothing that was scheduled or held while the page was hidden plays as a burst, and the music fades back in on its focus ramp (`MUSIC_FOCUS_TC_S`) with no click.

### How to reproduce

1. On a phone (iOS Safari and/or Android Chrome), open the client and start a game (`/practice` is enough). Tap until sound plays.
2. Mid-game, with music playing, leave the browser: go to the home screen or switch apps for a few seconds or longer.
3. Come back to the browser and tap the board.
4. Either nothing is audible from then on, or a harsh tear plays as the page returns.

### Where

`apps/web`, `apps/web/src/audio/`

### Leads (unconfirmed: verify before acting on them)

- `engine.ts` doesn't react to the page's lifecycle (`visibilitychange`, `pagehide`/`pageshow`, the context's `statechange`). Only the music player's focus gain (`music.ts` `browserFocus`) and the gesture unlock (`unlock.ts`) do. Everything else is left to the OS suspending and resuming the context.
- `unlock()` (`engine.ts`) only calls `ctx.resume()` on the existing context. If the OS closed it while the page was in the background (or it came back from the bfcache in a state `resume()` can't fix), nothing ever builds a new one. That would explain "audio doesn't come back". `state()` maps Safari's `"interrupted"` to `"suspended"`, so look at that path too.
- For the tear: anything scheduled against `ctx.currentTime` or by `setTimeout` while the page was hidden (music voices and fades, ducks, SFX, the focus gain's `setTargetAtTime`) may all fire or jump at once when the context resumes. Also check whether a gain ramp starts from a stale value.

### Acceptance

- Unit tests in `apps/web/src/audio/` with a fake `AudioContext` and document. The page goes hidden, then visible again, with the context `suspended`, `interrupted` and `closed`. After the next gesture, `engine.state()` is `"running"` and `playSfx` and the music play again. A closed context is rebuilt along with its mix and settings subscription.
